title: Linked List Journey
description: Pointer rewiring, fast/slow scans, cycles, list merging, doubly linked nodes, and LRU design.

journey.outcome: Rewire nodes without losing the remaining chain, and combine pointer invariants into practical list-based designs.

connections.middle-of-linked-list: Start with a read-only fast/slow scan. Moving one pointer twice as fast locates the midpoint without a preliminary length pass.
connections.reverse-linked-list: Move from reading links to changing them. Save the next unprocessed node before redirecting the current link, preserving access to the remaining chain.
connections.merge-two-sorted-lists: Keep a tail pointer for the already built result. The smaller current head is safe to append, and a dummy node removes special handling for the first result node.
connections.add-two-numbers: Reuse the output-tail construction while carrying arithmetic state between nodes. Unequal lengths and a final carry should follow the same loop invariant.
connections.remove-nth-node-from-end-of-list: Use two pointers with a fixed gap rather than different speeds. A dummy predecessor lets removal of the head use the same rewiring as any other node.
connections.linked-list-cycle: Return to fast/slow motion, now on a potentially cyclic chain. A repeated node identity matters; equal stored values do not establish a cycle.
connections.linked-list-cycle-ii: Extend cycle detection to locate its entry. After a meeting, restart one pointer at the head and move both one step at a time until their identities agree.
connections.intersection-of-two-linked-lists: Use shared node identity in two acyclic chains. Switching heads after reaching the end equalizes the total distance traveled despite different prefix lengths.
connections.palindrome-linked-list: Combine middle-finding and reversal: compare the first half with the reversed second half. Restore the list afterward when mutation is not part of the intended result.
connections.reorder-list: Reuse splitting and second-half reversal, but weave the halves together instead of comparing values. Cut the first half before merging so the old links cannot create a cycle.
connections.rotate-list: Make a temporary cycle deliberately, then break it at the new tail. Reduce the rotation by the list length and handle an unchanged rotation before rewiring.
connections.sort-list: Compose midpoint splitting with sorted merging into merge sort. Each recursive half must be physically separated and strictly smaller than its parent list.
connections.copy-list-with-random-pointer: A node now has more than one relationship. Separate creation of copied identities from wiring their next and random references so shared targets remain shared in the copy.
connections.reverse-nodes-in-k-group: Extend one reversal into repeated bounded segments. Verify a full group exists before changing it, then reconnect the previous tail and the untouched suffix.
connections.reverse-doubly-linked-list: Maintain both directions of every relationship. Swapping next and previous links at each node reverses the chain, but traversal must follow the saved original direction.
connections.lru-cache: Combine constant-time lookup with a doubly linked recency list. The map identifies a node directly, while unlinking and moving it preserves the least-to-most-recent ordering.

topics.name: Traversal and safe rewiring
topics.description: Find positions, preserve unprocessed nodes, and build results with a stable tail invariant.

topics.name: Cycles and shared identities
topics.description: Distinguish reference identity from equal values when chains meet or loop.

topics.name: Compose list operations
topics.description: Reuse splitting, reversal, and merging while reconnecting every affected boundary.

topics.name: Doubly linked design
topics.description: Maintain two-way links, then combine them with hashing for constant-time recency updates.
